title: REST API design
subtitle: Make requests, responses, and errors clear.
description: Design resources and HTTP status codes, validate DTOs, and return structured ProblemDetail errors. Document successful requests and edge cases.

lessons.title: Resource, HTTP method & status
lessons.summary: Model resources in URLs and use HTTP methods and status codes to describe the operation and its result.
objectives: Return a useful Location header when creating resources.
keyPoints: Use /orders for a collection and /orders/{id} for an individual resource.
GET, PUT, and DELETE are idempotent; POST needs an explicit strategy for safe retries.
201 Created should identify the new resource with Location.
practice: Creation returns 201 and Location; lookup returns 200 or 404.

exercises.prompt: POST /orders creates order 42. Which response best describes the result?
options: 201 Created with Location: /orders/42 and the order body.
exercises.explanation: 201 identifies a new resource and Location tells the client where to retrieve it.
An idempotent operation has the same intended server-side effect when repeated. POST does not guarantee this without additional handling.

exercises.prompt: Return 201 Created with Location /orders/{id} and the order as the body.
checks: Build the URI using the order ID
Include the order in the body
exercises.explanation: ResponseEntity.created(uri).body(order) sets the creation status and Location header.

lessons.title: DTO & Bean Validation
lessons.summary: DTOs define request and response data. Valid activates validation before input reaches the service.
objectives: Declare input constraints on a DTO.
Keep business checks in service or domain code.
keyPoints: NotBlank rejects null, empty, and whitespace-only strings.
Min(1) or Positive rejects non-positive quantities.
DTO constraints do not replace checks that require inventory or other state.
practice: Validate product and quantity in CreateOrderRequest and add Valid to the controller argument.
Invalid input returns 400 before the service is called.

exercises.prompt: Require a non-blank product and quantity of at least 1, then activate validation in the controller.
checks: Add Min(1) or Positive to quantity
Add Valid to the RequestBody parameter
exercises.explanation: Validation failure raises MethodArgumentNotValidException and returns 400 before entering the service.

exercises.prompt: Which is a business rule rather than a DTO format constraint?
options: Quantity must not exceed available inventory.
An email address must have a valid format.
exercises.explanation: Available inventory requires external state. Check it in service/domain code rather than a standalone input constraint.

lessons.title: Error response & ProblemDetail
lessons.summary: Use a consistent error format that clients can process and that does not expose internal details.
objectives: Map a domain exception to an HTTP response.
Return ProblemDetail for a missing resource.
Keep SQL errors and stack traces out of public responses.
keyPoints: ProblemDetail implements the Problem Details response format.
Use a correlation ID to connect a generic response with detailed server logs.
practice: Map OrderNotFoundException to a 404 ProblemDetail response.
The client gets a clear error without a stack trace or SQL details.

exercises.prompt: Write an advice handler that maps OrderNotFoundException to a 404 ProblemDetail using the exception message as detail.
exercises.explanation: The response uses application/problem+json and identifies the missing order with status 404.

exercises.prompt: Which database-failure response is safest to send to a client?
options: A 500 error with a generic message and reference ID 7f3a.
The full stack trace for debugging.
The raw SQL error including table, constraint, and key values.
exercises.explanation: Log detailed diagnostics on the server and send a correlation ID so the incident can be investigated without exposing internals.

lessons.title: API contract & edge cases
lessons.summary: Document payloads, status codes, headers, and failures so clients know what to handle.
keyPoints: Removing or renaming a response field breaks clients using it.
Making an optional request field required also breaks compatibility.
Malformed JSON should return 400 rather than an unrelated server error.
practice: Create repeatable curl examples for success, invalid input, missing tokens, and missing IDs.
The README states expected status codes, bodies, and headers.

options: Rename response field total to amount.
Add an optional note field to the response.
Make an optional coupon request field required.
exercises.explanation: Renaming fields or tightening required input changes assumptions existing clients depend on.

exercises.prompt: A client sends malformed JSON with no value after quantity. Which status is appropriate?
exercises.explanation: Spring maps unreadable JSON to 400. Do not accidentally turn this into 500 with an overly broad error handler.

exercises.prompt: Which response header identifies the new order after a 201 response?
exercises.hint: It tells the client the URI of the created resource.
exercises.explanation: Location points to the new resource, for example /orders/42.
